name: Naturalist's Delight - Better Scanning Rewards
summary: Twenty nanites for a rare creature? You deserve better.
author: Sibilantjoe
description:
[center][u]NATURALIST'S DELIGHT[/u]
[b]Better Scanning Rewards[/b]
Now updated for NEXT 1.55!


You've finally installed that last S-Class Scanner upgrade. You're getting millions of units for scanning those unique creatures and plants. Why shouldn't you get more nanites, too?



[b]Changes[/b]

Rewards for uploading discoveries is increased by [b]500%.
[/b]Optionally, you can use an alternative version that also increases monetary rewards for scanning:
Flora/Fauna: Small increase, but this still makes scanner upgrades much more effective.
Minerals: Now grants 10k Units instead of 200.

[b]Updates
[/b]Update 1.2: Reworked for NEXT 1.55 compatibility. Added standalone file "Geologist's Delight" for those who only want to change Mineral scan rewards.

[b][u]Installation

[/u][/b]Place either version (ONLY ONE!) of _NaturalistsDelight.pak in your mods folder (/GAMEDATA/PCBANKS/MODS).
(Create a MODS folder if one does not exist.)
Delete or rename "DISABLEMODS.TXT"

Note: This mod is incompatible with other mods that modify the DEFAULTREALITY.MBIN. That means you cannot use this along with the excellent [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/580]Nanites Available for Purchase[/url]﻿ mod. Sorry!

This mod was created using tub0crisco's No Man's Sky Modding Station[/center]

name: Better Planet Generation
summary: A huge planet generation overhaul that aims at making your hundreds of hours of exploration in the magnificent, infinite universe of No Man's Sky less repetitive and hopefully even more memorable.
author: WoodyMontana
description:
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][i][b]                                                     [size=6]Better Planet Generation[/size][/b][/i][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738968-1312445652.jpeg[/img]

[size=4][b]More planets

[/b][size=3]Better Planet Generation is a total overhaul of the planetary generation in No Man's Sky.[/size] [size=3]It improves by a significant margin the procedural aspect of the universe while at the same time respecting the original work and vision from Hello Games.[/size]

[size=3]It adds thousands of new distinct environments to the universe[/size][/size]. All of them come in five different life levels and varying placement scales and layouts. These environments were made to seamlessly combine with each other in many different ways.

Better Planet Generation is designed to bring variety to the different biomes you will visit but most of all it brings a lot of variation to the universe. Outside of the countless combinations of assets and their resulting new environments, planets you visit will present themselves differently each time. Placement layouts, scale of the regions, density, variety of assets and their respective scale, ...

No planet will look exactly the same. Unless, of course, it is a very simple one. More on that below.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1631005159-472402214.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-1789086190.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-1298994048.jpeg[/img]


[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=4][b]Sub Biomes[/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Caves and underwater sub biomes have also been entirely overhauled.

Tons of new variants have been added underground and just like on the surface, additional objects can spawn to increase variety even more.

﻿[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410276-924973523.jpeg[/img]﻿

Underwater has been completely revamped and is now generated through a triple layered dynamic framework combining assets to generate highly varied and detailed environments.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738939-165524032.jpeg[/img]
[b][size=4]
Unique planets

[/size][/b][size=4][size=3]On top of all the added variety, BPG also uses a flexible dynamic generation framework that can take many shapes[/size][/size] and create countless planetary variations, even when the same environments are being used multiple times.

Each planet generated has its own selection of parts based on its biome. Some liberties have been taken when designing and attributing those parts to the various biomes. Some objects have been injected to improve variety, but some restrictions have also been applied to preserve each biome's identity. Better Planet Generation also introduces countless restored, modified or repurposed assets to the game in order to increase the variety while preserving its visual style.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936068-132859967.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-754906087.jpeg[/img]

[/size][/size][/size][/size]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Natural Generation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is a vastly different experience compared to the unmodded game and even other biome mods.
Not even taking into account the small details, it is more than likely that you will never be able to encounter all the possible assets combinations this mod can generate. Let alone in the different regional layouts each dynamic template can result in.

Each biome has access to multiple procedural templates. Each producing different results in terms of layouts and objects combinations.
Their common goal is to show you a different kind of environment each time. Aesthetically and structurally.
No more "postcard" planets where most of what there is to see is right around the corner. The scale of the generation can get extremely vast compared to the vanilla game.

Planetary generation can now affect your visual enjoyment and the gameplay.
It is a video game, after all.

A world generated at its fullest possible level and highest complexity can take you some time to fully explore on foot. Meaning seeing the most notable regions (and not all of them) and scanning everything.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630052272-1155900954.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-2086924238.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630272224-118529207.jpeg[/img]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]More Variation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

On the other hand, Better Planet Generation also allows more simple, generic yet still visually interesting planets to see :

- Planets only covered in grass and some plants, rocks or both.
- More barren worlds dominated by giant stone or crystal spires.
- Radioactive wastelands.
- Planets dotted with trees or occasional small forests.
- Volcanic wastelands.
- Toxic fields.
- Rocky swamps.
- ...

And the list goes on and on.
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3]The occurence of these "generic" planets only relies on probabilites. None of my templates is designed to specifically produce them.
I made sure they still looked good, though.[/size][/size][/size][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410296-1590906166.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1626079315-1486130072.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Different Experience[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is not for everyone. Planets can be both very detailed in every aspect or very simple.
If you expect to always see trees and a full grass coverage on your Lush planet or anywhere else, there are other mods for that.
This is not what you should expect using BPG.

Now, whether you are a new player ready to explore an infinite universe or a more weathered one that wants to be surprised by the game again, I suggest you give Better Planet Generation a try. It won't harm your game in any way.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629923717-282604290.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410307-2137550589.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=5]WARNING BEFORE INSTALLING :[/size][/b]

Installing this mod will operate changes to the terrain in every biomes.
It is also recommended to install it while in a space station / anomaly / freighter and not on a planet's surface.
Some major updates to the mod can reset the terrain or biome lists.
I'll include a warning on the download page and the sticky when it's the case.[/size][/size][/size][/size]


Recommended :
[/size][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/968]DUD's Sky - Colors[/url] : load planetary colour palettes before BPG to avoid procedural textures conflicts.
[/size][/size]

name: Creature Distance
summary: Increases spawn distance of creatures and makes them easier to scan.
author: PacMan
description:
Based on Persistence Distance Creatures by TinFoilHead

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/364]https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/364[/url]

So far it hasn't been updated for Visions and I missed it so much I learned how to make the mod myself. I probably havent done as good as TinFoils version as I didn't want to mess with too many figures I didn't quite understand the consequences of. My version changes the following:

1 - Spawndistance of creatures are now 5x what they are by default. (acts the same as TinFoils)
2 - Creatures will spawn day and night regardless.
3 - Very rare creatures will spawn more often (not a lot but certainly more than what seems to be 1 creature per half a planet!).

I have tested this with 1.76 and have found no issues. I will keep the mod updated for as long as I use it.

Any problems let me know, although requests might be rejected until I understand the impacts better but feel free to ask. 

Will be incompatible with any mod that uses ROLEDESCRIPTIONTABLES folder.




[b]Extra credits[/b]
This mod can be based on the idea had by many many people over the past 2 years. It will be impossible to find them all. I have credited TinFoilHat as it was his mod that made me make this one, noone elses mod worked right for me when TinFoils did. Other mods out there that effect the spawn distance also effect other things that this mod doesn't or the other way round, none of these mods are exactly the same other than the premise that the creatures spawn further away.

If you had the same idea then please feel free to name yourself in the comments.

name: Exosolar's and Babs' Beyond Base Building
summary: ★ FULLY MP compatible, this mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options
author: Exosolar Sparky NeptuneX3 Babscoole
description:
[b][color=#f1c232][size=4]What is this Mod?[/size][/color][/b]
[size=4]There are now almost 1,000 buildable base parts in vanilla No Man's Sky! It's a dream come true!
This mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options.
This does NOT mean the mod gives you access to all buildable parts.  You still need to learn the blueprints for each.  :)
Beyond Base Building does NOT add any new build parts to the game.

Now includes all the functionality of gBase Items, [color=#ff0000]if chosen by running the Lua script[/color]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Can multiply power, extraction, and storage rates by 2, 5, or 10. WARNING: Bases built with this mod cannot be uploaded for multiplayer when using 2x, 5x, or 10x multiplied rates.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*][size=4]EM Generators do not need a hotspot and produce 250 power.  Not enabled by default.  Must run Lua through ANUMSS and answer question "Choose a multiplier for Storage and Rates and EMAnywhere status" to generate custom mod file to enable.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]

It is [b]fully compatible[/b] with multiplayer, co-op building, uploading, etc, because it [i]does not add[/i] any parts, which would cause issues in multiplayer.[/size]

[size=4][color=#f1c232][b]★ Beyond Basebuilding[/b] is fully Lua scripted, with script provided for easy updating and merging [b]★[/b][/color] and carries over all of the official updates and improvements offered by Hello Games [b]plus[/b]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Most parts can be Scaled [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] prefab building parts, [color=#fff2cc]Exocraft Geobays, Mineral/Gas Extractors and Base Computer[/color] (Door attachment points bug out when scaled, and issues persist with scaled base computers and geobays).  There may be others not listed.  Be aware, scaling breaks snapping.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built in a Freighter.  [color=#fff2cc][i]Exceptions[/i][/color]  include the Base Computer, Industrial Mining parts, Vehicle Summoners and planet-based teleporter.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built at a Planetary Base [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] the freighter teleporter and the Orbital Exocraft Materialiser[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can be built above and below water[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can change color and material[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts, which can be deleted, can be deleted without also deleting attached objects [color=#fff2cc][i]except[/i][/color] Decals and Posters[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]No build-count limits [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] for parts related to resources harvesting, certain terminals, beacons and message capsules (and others with limits that are hard coded into the game, as they are added or changed by Hello Games).[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Unlimited Storage Containers[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*This does not increase actual storage amounts: Each numbered container acts as an index to the store rather than a physical box[/i][/size][/color][/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Foundation, Pavings and Communications Station can be placed anywhere (not only on bare terrain)[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Non corvette parts buildable with corvettes[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]
Some customization of the mod is available just by running it through AMUMSS, where you'll be prompted about enabling several feature.  Even more customization can be had by editing the top portion of the Lua before processing.  See Lua usage below for link to AMUMSS install and basic usage How to.[/size]

[color=#f1c232][b][u][size=5]Disclaimer:[/size][/u][/b][/color]
[size=3]This MOD makes changes to the placement and usage setting of vanilla parts.  If the MOD is removed, the vanilla settings will be restored and parts that "violate" a vanilla setting as well as those connected may go "poof".  Best practice is to regularly backup your saves for semi-painless recovery from the unexpected.[/size]

[size=5][u][b][color=#f1c232]Is this Mod up-to-date?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4][i][b]Any mod files which are not hidden or demoted to the "Old Files" area can be expected to work.[/b][/i]
All uploaded files (on the Files page) are maintained with their packing date and version of the MBINCompiler used to pack it. Older mod versions, no longer compatible with the current version of No Man's Sky will be demoted to the "Old Files" subsection, but will remain available for download. There are no side-effects to using this mod.[/size]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]How to update, tweak, combine, or patch the mod with AMUMSS?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4]As this mod is now Lua scripted, you can [color=#fff2cc]easily [b]update[/b], [b]tweak[/b] or [b]merge[/b] the mod yourself[/color] (if a game update breaks this PAK of the mod, or you have other PAK or Lua mods that could conflict with this one). [color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*Click on the spoiler below for more[/i][/size][/color][/size]
[spoiler]
[size=3][u]Notes on AMUMSS:[/u]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] tries to update [url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler/releases]MBINcompiler[/url] automatically. If it fails to convert EXML/MBIN files, its likely due to a very recent NMS version update and MBINcompiler is awaiting an update too.
If so, I highly recommend you to disable your mods and wait for MBINCompiler to be updated (it's pretty quick in general).[/size]


[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Updating the mod after a game update:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][list]
[*] [size=3]Download [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url], and extract it locally,  avoid placing the AMUMSS folder in a path with special characters or in a system folder like [color=#fff2cc][i]"C:\Program Files (x86)\(...)"[/i][/color].[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Place the mod Lua script (only the .LUA file, not the .PAK file) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]AMUMSS will normally auto-detect the NMS installation folder, but you can also manually edit the path in the [color=#fff2cc][i]NMS_FOLDER.txt[/i][/color] file.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root of the AMUMSS folder and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]A new modded PAK file will be created, using the last update of the MBIN game files duly amended by the script.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]Most of the time simply recompiling the mod using the Lua script will make it compatible again. Use the latest script to ensure you adopt any mod adjustments to accommodate the latest NMS build.[/size][size=3] There are two main causes of mods not correctly updating with this method:
1) MBINCompiler needs an update to be able to decompile the latest version of the game MBIN files.
2) Structural changes have been made to the MBIN files called by this Lua script. Whilst unlikely, this will require some script rewrite and other mods are likely affected.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Tweaking the mod:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]Use the same process as described in [color=#fff2cc][i]Updating the mod[/i][/color].
Just modify the script as you want before recompiling it. Look at the top of my scripts, you can generally edit modifiers there, or even disable/enable some features very easily.[/size]

[size=3][color=#cccccc][i]*[url=https://notepad-plus-plus.org/]Notepad++[/url] or [url=https://code.visualstudio.com/download/]VSCode[/url] are generally recommended to read EXML and Lua files, due to large file support and automatic highlighting. The [url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/npp-compare/]Compare plugin[/url] for Notepad++, and Lua is also a must-have to highlight file differences.[/i][/color][/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Combining mods that provide Lua scripts:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You'll want to do this if multiple mods affect the same MBIN file.[/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Place all the scripts in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Follow the step, selecting that you want to combine all the scripts into one PAK file, and the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]AMUMSS will output a PAK file that will contain the modifications of all the scripts.[/size]
[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]*If the scripts modify the exact same values in the MBIN file, the last loaded script will overwrite the preceding script values.[/i][/size][/color][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Patch in the mod to make it compatible with other PAK files:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You will want to do this if another mods isn't Lua scripted, and affects the same MBIN file as the Lua scripted mod.

It will work when :
Case 1) you patch a Lua scripted mod for only one other PAK.
Case 2) you patch a Lua scripted mod for several other PAKs, but only if the other PAKs don't modify the same MBIN files between them.[/size]

[size=3][b]How to create a patched PAK:[/b][/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Copy the script and the other mod(s) PAK(s) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS, and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]The new PAK file will contain all the Lua script modifications, and a compatibility patch for the other mod(s) PAK(s).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Rename it something like [color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz Scripted Mod Name -Patched For- The Other Mod Name.pak"[/i][/color].[/size]
[size=3][color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz"[/i][/color] prefix is to ensure that it'll be loaded after the mod(s) it was patched for (for NMS loading order, underscore [i]"_"[/i] came after every other characters).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Remove the original scripted mod PAK from the [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder, and copy both the new patched one, and the other mod(s) PAK(s), into it.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=3][u]Notes:[/u]
[b]Be sure the mod PAK you want to create a compatibility patch for, is updated for the latest NMS version.[/b]
-> When AMUSS find an MBIN file affected by a script and by a PAK in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder, it will take the MBIN file from the mod PAK over the original one of the game, and will apply to it the modifications listed in the script.
So, if the MBIN file of the mod PAK is not updated, the one in the resulting patched PAK won't be either.[/size][/spoiler]
[/spoiler]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]
[color=#f1c232][u][b][size=5]Philosophy[/size][/b][/u][/color]
[size=4]All the erroneous limitations in building are pretty silly, aren't they? In making this mod, I paid specific attention to making sure I did not make changes that will invalidate the bases built with it from online play. Any base made with Beyond BaseBuilding will be fully viable and visible in online play, even when other players don't have this mod! It does this by only editing placement rules while you are in the building editor and not modifying any of the actual base parts themselves.

name: Quick Start
summary: Removes the tutorial mission at the start of the game.
author: Camus
description:
Quick Start removes the tutorial mission you would normally have to go through every time you start a new game in Normal, Survival or Permadeath. When you reach your ship you'll receive all the necessary blueprints for continued exploration and materials for constructing the hyperdrive. I didn't want to make things too easy though so you'll still need to repair the pulse drive and launcher with gathered materials. The story is set to start from chapter 2, so once you manage to leave your starting planet you'll gain immediate access to the Anomaly/Nexus.

name: Gnome Ann's Sky - 100000 New Skies
summary: Unhappy with the 6 (60 since Worlds Apart) day sky colours and single dusk sky colour in vanilla, this adds 100,000 skies. Made with calibration, love and alien influences...
author: Dr Kaii
description:
[b][color=#00ff00][size=6][center][font=Trebuchet MS][size=5][url=https://xkcd.com/1704/]﻿Gnome Ann[/url]﻿[/size][/font][size=5] has seen all 100K skies. It is Gnome Ann's sky after all...[/size][/center][/size][/color][/b]The Cursed Update (5.21)[size=5]
Important: The skies file is now independent of the 4x day/night (and its less storms variant).
If you want 4x day/night (or 4x day/night + storms) you need 2 mod .paks in your MODS folder:
eg [b][color=#ff0000]DRKAII_GnomeAnnsSky100K V3 [Aquarius].pak[/color][/b][b][color=#616161]AND [/color][color=#ff0000]DRKAII_4x Day Night Cycle Length + Less Storms.pak[/color][/b]
[/size]
[size=4][u]About This Mod[/u][/size]

Changes (only) the sky colours (which includes sky, clouds, fog, sunlight). This is a mod made with love and care, that Gnome Ann has shown before. Dozens of hours have gone in to carefully putting together a sky generation algorithm, that is calibrated and fine tuned to produce 100K skies that mean you never know what kind of world you are going to land on next, but isn't going to change the game drastically. It does this by:

[list]
[*]Generating 100,000 skies in various levels of "rarity".
[*]The most common skies are made in the bright, not overly vivid "pastel colours" style of vanilla, with white clouds, tame single colours and nice and bright. However, unlike vanilla, they can be almost any colour!
[*]There are progressively more rare and more interesting colours, all the way up to truly bizarre alien skies [font=Trebuchet MS]Gnome Ann[/font] has imagined.
[*]No type of sky is truly ruled out. Expect to find not just beauty on your travels, but the ugly, the harsh, the dim and the most alien skies imaginable. 
[*]Even among the different planet types produced by the algorithm, there are sub-types leading to almost endless variety. 
[*]Given that there are more skies than you can ever see, and anything is possible, this is truly in the spirit of the game - an explorer's dream mod. 
[*]Takes ideas from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/58018181]Exosolar[/url]'s [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1342]Stratos[/url]﻿ mod as well as the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/947]Atlas Alien Skies mod[/url]﻿ by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/41291360]moddinaccount[/url], but is made from scratch with a unique, hand crafted generation algorithm. You might find the starry-daytime skies similar to Stratos, and the multicoloured vivid alien skies of Alien Skies, and sometimes both! 
[/list]

[u][size=4]Associated Mods[/size]
[/u][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1805][img]data:image/png;base64,[/img][/url]     [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1848/][img]data:image/png;base64,[/img][/url]﻿  [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1879][img]https://i.imgur.com/j9yh5cj.png[/img][/url]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1805]Gnome Ann's Dusks[/url] - adds 1,000 sunsets produced under the same method and philosophy
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1848/]1,000 Gnome Ann's Nights[/url] - adds 1,000 nights produced under the same method and philosophy
[b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1879]NMS Collections Backup & Restore Tool[/url][/b] - Want to be able to save planets in an easy way, bookmarked with thumbnails/descriptions, and revisit them at the click of a button, as well as share with a large NMS discord? This is the tool for you. Also lets you backup bases, companions, ships and much more!

[size=4][u]Key points[/u]:[/size]
[list=1]
[*][size=2]By far the most skies - you'll [i]never [/i]see them all, and very unlikely you'll see the same one twice - very NMSy.[/size]
[*][size=2]Simple - only uses 1 globals file, very compatible with other mods and only affects skies. [/size]
[*][size=2]Author is committed to preserving skies per planet. You pick a home, I will do my best to make sure its sky never changes (if HG doesn't bork things).[/size]
[*][size=2]Designed in the spirit of NMS, using a calibrated algorithm to make procedural skies. [/size]
[*][size=2]Contains the most variety of sky possibilities, yet aims to appeal to most with a majority of skies in the style of NMS (yet anything is possible, including starry day time skies and ridiculous alien skies!).[/size]

[/list]
The other Sky mods are excellent too, and are made by very respected modders who I learned from and look up to. Do check them all out! Some are designed more deliberately with pallets and artistic talent, like Exosolar's Stratos, or are made in combination with more comprehensive biome changes like Dud's, or come with lots of options like Atlas Alien Skies. Whatever speaks to you, if it's not Gnome Ann's Sky, it's [i]your [/i]sky.


[size=4][u]Philosophy of Mod[/u][/size]

This mod is born out of [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQuH7RrZ6Io]frustration[/url]. Since Next, the number of colours the sky can be in a game dedicated to exploring the infinite is a very finite 6 (it took 7 years for them to add another 54 skies bringing the total to 60, in World Apart). Anyone who is into their exploring and planet churning will know that this quickly proves fatal to the explorer's spirit. It is clear that HG intend to one day flesh this out, but until then, for those that can't wait, here is a mod that is designed to give your explorer's heart its beat back. Every planet you explore from now on will be utterly unique in its "feel" and "atmosphere". You never know what you are going to run into next.

Given that the mod is tuned to produce a majority of skies that are quite tame, very vanilla-esque, it won't ruin the game. It should appeal to most. However, there is a very good chance you will find...well anything. The algorithm has been tuned to rule out a fair chunk of nonsense skies and ones that are too dark etc. but otherwise, any colour and colour-combination is possible, and there are even some bonus styles that may pop up from time to time that are truly out there. 
All being said, this mod has been tuned to try to appeal to as many people as possible, and not be too niche. 

This mod was also made with the philosophy that almost any type of sky can exist. Any combination of chemicals in the atmosphere, any thickness/density of atmosphere is possible, even the clouds and fog can take on almost any colours. This is technically true, even in real life, but especially in the world of No Man's Sky. If this bothers you and you feel colours possibilities can't be too unrestrained, this is not the mod for you!

[size=4][u]How the Mod was Made

[/u][/size]This mod was made with a custom program to generate all the colour values the game accepts based on a very complex algorithm. A tool was used to visualise the results to help fine tune the algorithm. The result is infinite colours and combinations, but tamed to make [font=Trebuchet MS]Gnome Ann[/font] happy. Very personalised and unique. 

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/JrZBoC65En9by9llTo/giphy.gif[/img]

[b]The mod will likely [i]improve [/i](while avoiding significant [i]change[/i])[/b]. You should check for updates, and if you notice something bad, you can feel free to let me know.

This mod has been made by a colour and coding enthusiast, over the course of a week and dozens of hours, but certainly not made by a professional or expert in any of the relevant fields. Just think what HG can do if (and when) they invest the man hours to making their own colour variety!

Will be releasing the tool to help you generate your own skies eventually, once I've made it useful to the wider public as right now it's geared towards a specific design and will stifle your creativity. 

[size=4][u]Things to Note[/u] (PLEASE READ)[/size]

[list]
[*]This mod will change your planets' skies (while installed,[b] they will revert if you uninstall[/b], even if you've saved). There's no way a mod can be set to keep the skies of specific planets but change others. For that reason, you might want to start a new save.
[*]This mod isn't perfect. There will be some colour combinations that suck. For example, some colours make the clouds look weird, but that's hard to predict. Recent update has drastically improved this, reducing the splotchy clouds by a lot
[*]You are not going to like some (hopefully rare) colours, that's just the way it is. People are very unique with what they like and dislike about colours. Some get a headache from a yellow sky, some from red. Some think too vivid = very very bad, some love the possibility. Take it as it is, but bear in mind it's been tuned with the philosophy to appealing to as many people as possible.
[*]Note that you might get unlucky. You might find your first 10 planets are all extreme skies. It might ruin all your bases with very alien skies. Do note that most skies are tame.
[*]The goal is to never ever change the sky colours in future (if it can be avoided, Hello Games will probably one day permanently break this mod as they update and improve the game). This is also why there is and will only ever be [b][u]one core variation[/u][/b]. Any change to the skies in the mod will mean all the planets get assigned (procedurally) another colour. So all your favourite planets and bases will change. This is why change will be [i]avoided at all costs[/i].
[*]This mod, unpacked, is over 250Mb. It may cause loading issues on slower rigs (tested on SSD). Please let me know if this is the case.
[*]If you wish to see this combined with any other mods that use the GCSKYGLOBALS.GLOBALS.MBIN, let me know and if enough people ask, I will add it.
[*]The aim is to always keep this mod maintained!
[/list]
[u]Change Log[/u]

[b]As of 16-Feb-2020[/b]
[list]
[*]Adjusted the clouds so that there are far less pure white clouds
[*]Added more colour variation to the clouds
[*][s]Changed a setting to reduce the fog, to make distant mountains more visible and hopefully reduce the blow-out of the clouds a bit (see above)[/s] [code][removed][/code]
[*]Added a variant that adds 1,000 custom nights over the single vanilla night. In this variant, the dusks are darker because the dusks become the night. It is recommended you try both, especially if you are a fan of the original dusks. Big thanks to [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/58018181]Exosolar[/url] for discovering and explaining how to do this to me. 
[*]Fixed the lighting of some dusks that would make the ground pitch black (currently for the nigh-version only, a fix for the standard dusks is coming soon). 
[/list]
[b]As of Living Ship Update[/b]
[list]
[*]Made sure all Custom Nights versions had night skies that were transparent (i.e. can see stars at night)
[*]Brightened the extremely dark lighting on a small percentage of dusks in the standard (i.e. NOT Custom Nights) versions
[/list][b]
As of 23-Feb-2020[/b]
[size=4]MAJOR UPDATE. Splotchy blown out clouds reduced by a lot. Extremely white featureless clouds reduced >90%. Lots more colour added to clouds (feedback requested if it's too much).

[u][color=#ffff00]CHANGES TO THE MOD WITH ORIGINS[/color][/u]:

[list]
[*][s][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/992]Less Storms[/url]﻿ modules removed (for now).[/s] [b]Less Storms is back! Storms will not be more frequent than every 45 minutes or less than every 60 minutes.[/b]
[*][s]Nights modules removed (for now).[/s]
[*]Still includes a version that retains the 4x length day/night cycle of the
old Less Storms module (day is 1 hour, night is 1 hour real time)[*]Vanilla game now has per-biome skies, although it seems limited to only about
20, and only for Lava and Swamp sub-biomes (could be more complicated, but this is what I've been able to figure out so far). This mod removes all that and effectively allows any sky to appear on any planet. NOTE: this was necessary to prevent changing the per-planet sky colours the mod applied from pre-Origins.[/list][u][color=#00ff00]COMING VERY SOON[/color][/u] (ETA October - track this mod!):

[list]
[*][s]Will try to bring back Less Storms modules.[/s] ✅
[*][s]Will brighten the dusks again now that they don't need to also act as the night skies.[/s]✅
[*][s]Will make a new nights version that takes advantage of the new night skies file.[/s] ✔️ (test version available in misc files)
[/list][/size]
[list]
[*]Dusks were also moved to their own [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1805]mod[/url]﻿ around this time. 
[/list][b][color=#00ff00][size=5]V2:[/size]
[/color][/b]I have noticed that too many of the skies are overly vivid/saturated. More than I had intended. Some have complained. I have run a pass on all the skies to reduce the saturation where it is too high (although not all). I have done the same with the clouds, as some are just too saturated and it creates burnout.

Specifically, I have measured the saturation as a % of every sky colour in the list, and if it is over 70%, I reduced the saturation by 50% (which is less than it sounds), 85% of the time (i.e. I left 15% of very vivid skies untouched). I also did roughly the same thing with the clouds, but over 60% saturation. 

Note, all I've done is desaturate, so your favourite planets shouldn't look very different, a rather small percentage will look just a bit more pastel, but the same colour. If you are strongly against me replacing the main mod because this has actively ruined your base etc (very unlikely!), please let me know in the discussion. I will listen.

[b][size=5][u]UPDATE To V3[/u]:
[/size][/b][size=5]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/vfW4PyZ.jpg[/img]﻿
[/size]
[size=3]Too many planets had very thick, vivid fog. This was an unfortunate result to some changes HG made to the fog effects, back when Origins dropped, but it took me a while to notice. I've run a pass on 85% of all skies with overly saturated fog, and desaturated them by 70%. 

This is still subject to change, as I might need to increase or decrease the effect. If you wish to test another version that doesn't desaturate as strongly, please use the mod in the subfolder attached.

Also, I have run a pass on any skies that have very dark lighting, increasing it. There are some rare planets I baked in that are quite dark during the day, with very vivid clouds. On some of those, the lighting was way too dark, and so I've hopefully fixed that.

Please provide feedback on the discussion tab or by email: kaii@dr.com

Thanks![/size]

name: NomNom
summary: NomNom is the most complete savegame editor for NMS but also shows you additional information around the data you're about to change. You can also easily look up each item individually to examine its attributes, independently of a savegame, or get other useful information that are not related to a specific one (but enhanced if one is loaded).
author: zencq
description:
[color=#e69138][size=3][b]NomNom is now in beta state.[/b] This means for you that some things may still not be 100% finished but the general state of the tool is a lot better than before.[/size] If you encounter bugs or when you think something doesn't work as expected or could be improved, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1566?tab=bugs]let me know[/url]![/color]

[color=#ff0000]All available features are tested while implemented but mistakes can happen, so be aware of that and backup your saves![/color]

The features can be divided into the different main parts:
[list]
[*][b]Manager[/b] Manage your saves![list]
[*]Automatic backup.
[*]Save your save as human-readable JSON.
[*]Copy, move, and swap slots to another.
[*]Delete your save.
[/list]
[*][b]Editor[/b] Edit your save for your needs![list]
[*]Ability to manage fleets, change data values like currencies and stats, and organize inventories.
[*]Ability to fast travel to any system you like, trigger space battles, and clear portal interference.
[*]Ability to edit your knowledge and recorded experiences.
[/list]
[/list]
Have a look at the screenshots as well, to see what NomNom is capable of.

Each version of NomNom is built with the latest game version (at that time) in mind and the version number is reflecting that. Each one is also backwards
compatible down to [b]Beyond 2.11[/b] and even saves before that can still be edited via the build-in JSON editor. If you use it with a newer game version branch than
the one it was built for (e.g. [b]7.00[/b]), things should work as usual in most cases but there can always be a breaking change.

NomNom is compatible with every platform No Man's Sky is available on (some work better than others though). You can select a specific account/folder with you saves or, for platforms on PC, one level above if you have multiple accounts. A complete and always up-to-date overview with additional notes can be found [url=https://github.com/zencq/libNOM.io?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started]on GitHub[/url].


[b]Instructions[/b][list=1]
[*]After downloading and extracting the zip file you'll find a few files. All you need to care about is the executable ([b]NomNom.exe[/b]) but new folders may    be created at runtime (e.g. for backups) that will become relevant to you.
[*]You may want to create a shortcut to the executable for easier access.
[*]As the tool includes an automatic backup functionality you don't need to do it manually but if you want to be absolutely safe, do it.
[*]At first start the tool locates your saves at the default location of each platform but if that fails, you must select it manually.
[*]Select a slot.
[*]Start tinkering!
[/list]

If you like NomNom and want to support me in its further development, you can do so via the donation options above or on [url=https://www.buymeacoffee.com/cengelha]Buy Me a Coffee[/url], [url=https://github.com/sponsors/cengelha]GitHub[/url], [url=https://ko-fi.com/cengelha]Ko-fi[/url], and [url=https://www.patreon.com/cengelha]Patreon[/url]. I will appreciate it!
There won't be a paywall though.

The is also a dedicated [url=https://discord.gg/nomnom-762409407488720918]Discord[/url] server where you'll find all information in one place, firsthand. Please read the rules first, to gain full access. If you need (or want to offer) help, found a bug, have a suggestion, or something else regarding NomNom, you will find, or can post it there.

Issues created here on Nexus Mods or via another channel will of course also be addressed.


Header image by [url=https://patreon.com/Orioto]Orioto[/url]﻿.

name: Trading Post Adjustments
summary: Contains options to add more landing pads, add a Ship Salvage Terminal, and let NPCs use all the landing pads at Trading Posts.
author: revaneldaris9
description:
Contains three main options, which can be installed together or separately.  

Can also be installed/updated via a .lua script provided by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/73745558]Makto[/url].

[b]More Landing Pads:[/b]
Adds three more landing pads in front of the current three to every trading post, bringing the total number up to 10.

MoreLandingPads+3.pak
Edits MODELS\PLANETS\BIOMES\COMMON\BUILDINGS\TRADINGPOST\PARTS\TRADINGPOST_COMMON.SCENE

[b]Ship Salvage Terminal: [/b]
Adds a Ship Salvage Terminal to every trading post, allowing upgrading/scrapping of ships without having to go to the Space Station.

TPShipSalvageStations.pak
Edits MODELS\PLANETS\BIOMES\COMMON\BUILDINGS\TRADINGPOST\LAYOUTS\
LAYOUT_SCIENTIFIC.SCENE
LAYOUT_TRADER.SCENE
LAYOUT_WARRIOR.SCENE

[b]NPCs Use All Landing Pads:[/b]
A quick edit to allow NPCs to use all the landing pads at Trading Posts. This will also cause NPCs to fill all the available spots on space stations and inside freighters, but not the player-built landing pads.

NPCsUseAllLandingPads.pak
Edits GCAISPACESHIPGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN.


Working as of Companions patch 3.31.

A big thanks to [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/29026665]JJhookah[/url]﻿ for their help with editing the trading post, I would recommend their [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1057]Trading Post Revamp[/url] for a more detailed and thorough overhaul. 

Please report any issues or problems. Enjoy!

name: Inventory Rebalance
summary: A small mod that tweaks inventory size for Normal and Survival/Permadeath
author: jackty89
description:
[size=5][b]Description[/b][/size]

[size=4]This mod aims to rebalance the inventory and tech size in a more balanced way.
I went crazy on Normal as I personally play survival mode more and even the 9999 stack size were "easy mode" for me so making them larger didn't affect me in any way.
For survival I tried to balance it out a bit more adding just a bit to each next step.
Lua and CS (NMSMB) scripts are available as seperate downloads.[/size]

[line]
[size=5][b]Technical Details[/b][/size]

[size=4][b]Files Changed[/b][/size]
[quote]
[list]
[*]METADATA/GAMESTATE/DIFFICULTYCONFIG.MBIN
[/list][/quote]
[size=4][b]Mod Format Explantion[/b][/size]
[quote]
[b]EXML Format:[/b] [u]Partial edit[/u], only touches the lines/values that need editing. Very low chance of conflicts with other mods (unless they edit the same values). Can be edited easily by user using an editor like Notepad ++/VSCODE/... .
[b]MBIN Format:[/b] [u]Full File Replacement[/u]. High chance of conflict, comparable with old pak format (pre. WORLDS). Can be used together with EXML, MBIN mods are loaded first so changes in EXML mods that edit the same file will still be applied. Other MBIN mods that change the same file follow the FIFO principle, merging is highly recommended with MBIN mods (see How To).
[b]Lua Format:[/b] Script file used by AMUMSS to generate the mod or used for merging.
[b]CS Format:[/b] Script file used by NMSMB to generate the mod or used for merging.[/quote]
[size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size]
[quote]
[b]Install path:[/b] ...\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS
[b]How to install:[/b] Recommend installation is manual, vortex can be used but some mods contain multiple versions so user might need to delete files/folders. Common steps, download mod, extract the file(s) from archived file and copy to the install path.[/quote]
[line]
[size=5]Mod Details[/size]
[quote]
[b][u]Mod Format:[/u][/b] Full EXML
[b][u]InventoryRebalance (Choose one)[/u][/b]
For Normal the changes include
[list]
[*]Exosuit Inventory: 50 000
[*]Exosuit Products: 50
[/list][list]
[*]Cargo Inventory: 100 000
[*]Cargo Products: 100
[/list][list]
[*]Ship Inventory: 50 000
[*]Ship Products: 50
[*]Freighter Inventory: 100 000
[*]Freighter Products: 100
[*]Container Inventory: 100 000
[*]Container Products: 100
[/list]
For Survival/Perma the changes include
[list]
[*]Exosuit Inventory: 500
[*]Exosuit Products: 5
[*]Exosuit Cargo: 1000
[*]Exosuit Cargo Products: 10
[*]Ship Inventory: 2000
[*]Ship Products: 10
[*]Freighter Inventory: 5000
[*]Freighter Products: 25
[*]Container Inventory: 5000
[*]Container Products: 25
[/list]
[b][u]InventoryUnbalance (Choose one)[/u][/b]
For all gamemodes
[list]
[*]Exosuit Inventory: 50 000
[*]Exosuit Products: 2 500
[/list][list]
[*]Cargo Inventory: 100 000
[*]Cargo Products: 5 000
[/list][list]
[*]Ship Inventory: 50 000
[*]Ship Products: 2 500
[*]Freighter Inventory: 100 000
[*]Freighter Products: 5 000
[*]Container Inventory: 100 000
[*]Container Products: 5 000
[/list]
[size=3][color=#ff0000][b]WARNING: if the mod breaks any item or substance that is over the vanilla limit will be gone.[/b][/color][/size][/quote]
[line]
[size=5]Extra information[/size]

name: Alternative Vehicle Control
summary: The files included here will allow a player to re-enable Alternative Vehicle Control (keyboard input) and a choice of alternative keyboard mappings for it. This disables vehicle movement with the mouse, while still controlling view.
author: Devilin Pixy
description:
The following is available for download, make sure to read carefully.

[size=5][b]Alternative Vehicle Control[/b] (patch mod/exml)[/size]
Enables Alternative Vehicle Control for vehicle movement with keyboard instead of mouse.
[size=3][b][i]Note[/i][/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Alters the following source file: [b]GCVEHICLEGLOBALS.MBIN[/b]
[/list]
[line]
[size=5][b]Disable KeyP[/b] (replacement mod/mbin)[/size]
Disables the default use of the P key (keyboard), while leaving the alternative Escape key input for the same functionality in-tact. Useful for those who wish to map the P key to something else, or required for those using Alternative Vehicle Control with a mapping that uses the P key.
[size=3][b][i]Note[/i][/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Alters the following source file: METADATA\INPUT\BINDINGS\[b]GCINPUTBINDINGS_WIN_KEYBOARD.MBIN[/b]
[/list]
[line]
[size=5][b]Alternative Vehicle Control and Disable KeyP[/b] (above combined)[/size]
A combination of both the above mods Alternative Vehicle Control and Disable KeyP.
[size=3][b][i]Note[/i][/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Alters the following source files:  [b]GCVEHICLEGLOBALS.MBIN[/b] and METADATA\INPUT\BINDINGS\[b]GCINPUTBINDINGS_WIN_KEYBOARD.MBIN[/b]
[/list]
[line]
[size=5][b]Vehicle Control - Arrow Keys[/b] (replacement mod/mbin/keyboard mapping)[/size]
Custom keyboard mapping for vehicle control using the arrow keys.
[size=3][b][i]Requires[/i][/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Alternative Vehicle Control
[/list][size=3][b][i]Note[/i][/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Alters the following source file: METADATA\ENGINESETTINGS\[b]TKGAMESETTINGS.MBIN[/b]
[*]Also available as a separate file to manually overwrite your current TKGAMESETTINGS
[/list]
[line]
[size=5][b]Vehicle Control - P L ; ' Keys[/b] (replacement mod/mbin/keyboard mapping)[/size]
Custom keyboard mapping for vehicle control using the P L ; ' keys.
[size=3][b][i]Requires[/i][/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Alternative Vehicle Control and Disable KeyP
[/list][size=3][b][i]Note[/i][/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Alters the following source file: METADATA\ENGINESETTINGS\[b]TKGAMESETTINGS.MBIN[/b]
[*]Also available as a separate file to manually overwrite your current TKGAMESETTINGS
[/list]
[line]
[size=5][b]How to Install Mods[/b] [b]5.50+ [/b](.mbin / .exml)[/size]
[list=1]
[*]Download the mod(s) from Nexus Mods.
[*]Unzip/decompress the downloaded file(s).
[*]Place the full extracted content folder in "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS\...".
Make sure to [b]NOT / NO LONGER[/b] use "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS\..." !!!
[*]If you have multiple mods, make sure they are not conflicting when altering the same source file(s).

[/list][b]Note: [/b]For full details about modding since Worlds Part II (5.50), please check this [url=https://docs.google.com/document/d/18k5VfvzLXbpBrAGGO7LK30c2Ta_lWQ5F5YgEpuwKZ6M]Google Doc[/url]﻿.
[line]
[size=5][b]How to Install Mods[/b] [b]pre-5.50 [/b](.pak files only)[/size]
[list=1]
[*]Download the .pak file(s) from Nexus Mods.
[*]Place the .pak file(s) in "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS\..."
Make sure to [b]NOT[/b] use "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS\..."
[*]Delete or rename the DISABLEMODS.txt file in "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\..."
[*]If you have multiple mods, make sure they are not conflicting when altering the same source file(s).
[/list]
[line]
[size=5][b]How to use Custom Mappings[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]When using a mod
[list]
[*]Make sure the mod is installed correctly
[*]After making a backup of the TKGAMESETTINGS.MXML file in the following location, delete it: "No Man's Sky\Binaries\Settings\..."
[b]Note[/b]: This will delete any custom key mappings you may have had already! You might want to add these back again after.[*]Launch No Man's Sky and it should generate the new custom keyboard mapping.
[/list][*]When doing this manually
[list]
[*]Make a backup of the TKGAMESETTINGS.MXML file in the following location: "No Man's Sky\Binaries\Settings\..."
[*]Open the TKGAMESETTINGS.MXML file in any text editor
[*]Edit your keyboard mappings manually.
You can use the downloads I made available as a template.
[b]Note[/b]: When you create custom mappings, make sure you do this right. Feel free to ask any questions.[/list][/list]
[line]
[size=5][b]LUA files[/b][/size]
LUA files are available for download in the 'Miscellaneous' section. These can be used with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] in case of conflicts with other mods.They were created by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/62067056]Babscoole[/url].

[line]
[size=5][b]Fair Warning[/b][/size]
I do not hold myself responsible for using my mods or otherwise making changes to the game.

[*]Mods can break with an update.

name: Simple EXML Merger
summary: inputフォルダ内を走査し.EXMLファイルをマージしながらoutputフォルダにまとめるツール。
author: cielmer9
description:
いろいろMODを入れていったらロードが遅くなってしまったので、それを解消するために自分向けに作ったツールです。
そこそこ意図したとおりに動いてくれると思います。

1. 必要なもの
このコードは Python（3.x系）で動作します。

2. 使い方
コマンドラインから起動してください。
[code]python merge_mods.py[/code]
.pyファイルのパスを基準に動作するようにしているので、
カレントを意識せずとも問題ありません。

3. 仕様
・inputフォルダ内のサブフォルダを再帰的に走査し、outputフォルダにコピーします。
　→.EXML ファイルかつ対象ファイルが複数存在する場合は、XML パースして各要素をマージします。
　→.EXML ファイル以外はそのままコピーします。
・マージ処理時に同じ要素があった（競合した）場合、あとから来たほうの値で上書きます。
・outputフォルダにmerged_yyyymmddhhmmssフォルダが作成されます。
　→yyyymmddhhmmssは実行時の年月日時分秒が入ります。
　→このmergedフォルダをNMSのMODフォルダにコピーしてください。
・競合した要素をconflict.logに出力します。
・処理した内容をapp.logに出力します。
・outputフォルダ内にmergedフォルダが複数存在する場合、前回実行分はzip圧縮して3世代保持します。
　→圧縮時に.logファイルも一緒に梱包します。
　→未圧縮の.logファイルは1世代保持（直近1回分のみ）です。
・その他、細かい仕様は.pyファイルのコードやコメントを読んでください。

4. 実例
例えばinputフォルダ内がこんな感じのとき、

[code]﻿D:\SIMPLE EXML MERGER\INPUT
├─MOD1
│  └─globals
│          gcplayerglobals.global.EXML
│
├─MOD2
│  └─GLOBALS
│          GCPLAYERGLOBALS.GLOBAL.EXML
│
├─MOD3
│  └─METADATA
│      └─SIMULATION
│          └─MISSIONS
│              └─TABLES
│                      MISSIONTABLE.MBIN
│
└─MOD4
    └─GLOBALS
            GCSPACESHIPGLOBALS.GLOBAL.EXML
[/code]
ツールを実行するとoutputフォルダ下がこんな感じになります。

[code]﻿D:\SIMPLE EXML MERGER\OUTPUT
└─merged_yyyymmddhhmmss
    ├─GLOBALS
    │      GCPLAYERGLOBALS.GLOBAL.EXML
    │      GCSPACESHIPGLOBALS.GLOBAL.EXML
    │
    └─METADATA
        └─SIMULATION
            └─MISSIONS
                └─TABLES
                        MISSIONTABLE.MBIN
[/code]
5. 免責
・実行は自己責任で。
・あんまり深い要素のある.EXMLファイルの場合、マージの挙動が気に食わないことがあると思います。
　そのときはconflict.logを見ながら手動で調整するなり、そのMODだけ手でマージするなりしてください。
　後から来た値を採用するので、inputフォルダ内のサブフォルダの名前を調整するのも有効です。

name: Starship Trail Tweaks
summary: Makes the engine trails shorter, or removes them completely if the installed trail has other particle effects.
author: Saltifisu
description:
[size=5][u]FEATURES[/u][/size]

[size=3]This mod aims to make the ship engine effects less obnoxious by making them way shorter or removing the trail completely. 

[/size][list]
[*][size=3]Shorter trails for Normal, Emeril, Cadmium, Golden, Stealth, and Chromatic trails (configurable, instructions below).[/size]
[*][size=3]Removes trail completely for Sputtering, Temporal and Plasma trails, but keeps the particle effects.[/size]
[/list]

[quote][size=5][u]IMPORTANT![/u]
[/size]
[size=3]Trail length is tied to frame rate! There's three preconfigured versions of this mod. One is meant for 80 fps and under, one for frame rates between 80 and 165, and one for above 165. If you use the low frame rate mod with unlimited frame rate, you might not see any trails at all. If you use a high frame rate version and get low fps in game, the trails will not appear any shorter than unmodded trails. [/size]

[size=4][u]

IF YOUR TRAILS FLICKER
[/u]
[/size][size=3]Cap your frame rate. As said, trail length is tied to frame rate, and unstable fps will show up as flickering. This is vanilla behavior, but it's hidden because the ends of the trails are normally not visible on screen.[/size][/quote]

[size=5][u]Compatibility[/u][/size][size=5][u]

[/u][/size][size=2]This mod only modifies two lines of code in every .TRAIL files via EXML edits, so it should be compatible with 99% of other mods.


[/size][quote][size=5][u]Optional Settings[/u][/size][size=2]
[/size]
Want longer trails? or no trails at all?


[u][size=3]For AMUMSS:
[/size][/u][size=2]
The provided LUA file has a few variables with explanations you can use to tweak the mod to your liking[/size][size=3].[/size][u][size=3]


For manual modding:
[/size][size=2]
[/size][/u][size=2]You'll need to tweak a few files manually depending of which trail you are using. [/size][size=3]
[/size][list]
[*][size=2]Go to "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS\Starship Trail Tweaks v1.0\MODELS\EFFECTS\TRAILS\SPACECRAFT\HOT"[/size]
[*][size=2]Edit the file for the engine you wish to modify:[/size]
[list]
[*]HOTTRAIL.TRAIL.EXML is for [size=2]Normal, Emeril, Cadmium, Golden and Stealth trails. I could separate these to their own files, but it could lead to issues with mod compatibility. Message me if you need separated controls for these trails for some reason.[/size]
[*][size=2]RAINBOWTRAIL.TRAIL.EXML is for Chromatic trail.[/size]
[*][size=2]SPUTTERINGTRAIL.TRAIL.EXML is for Sputtering trail.[/size]
[*][size=2]TIMELOOPTRAIL.TRAIL.EXML is for Plasma trail.[/size]
[*][size=2]PLASMATRAIL.TRAIL.EXML is for Temporal trail.[/size] ﻿
[/list][/list]Plasma and Temporal trails don't behave well with shorter trail lengths so I would leave those off...

[u][size=3]Edits:

[/size][/u][size=2]Width: Controls the width of the trail. Accepts decimals. [/size][u][size=3]
[/size][/u][size=2]Points: Controls the length of the trail.[/size][size=3] [/size][size=2]Values under 3 produce no trail. Does not accept decimals.[/size][/quote][u][size=3]

[/size][/u][size=5][u]Installation
[/u][/size]
[list]
[*]Unzip the file
[*]Paste the folder to "[size=2]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS" (NOT "\PCBANKS\MODS"!)[/size]
[*][size=2]Some zipping utilities (looking at you 7zip) can create an additional folder layer when unzipping files. Make sure your folder structure is "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS\Starship Trail Tweaks v1.0\MODELS..." And [u]NOT[/u] [size=2]"No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS\Starship Trail Tweaks v1.0\[size=2][size=2]Starship Trail Tweaks v1.0\[/size][/size]MODELS..."[/size][/size]
[/list]

name: Fast Locate Assistant for Ship Hunting (FLASH)
summary: Flexible Ship Hunting Assistant to help find ships faster by allowing you to limit ship types being spawned; by default, only Exotics can spawn, but other combinations can be selected. Does NOT alter default seeds at all, so ship hunters can safely share their coordinates with vanilla players. AMUMSS-compatible Lua available and simple to tweak.
author: DarkScythe and Babscoole
description:
[u]Note:[/u]
[color=#ea9999]This mod is not able to help with finding the new Sentinel/Interceptor ships.[/color]
Or crashed ship hunting in general.

This is because Interceptors must be found via the crashed ship mechanic, which functions differently from ships that are flown around by NPC's, which this mod targets instead.
This is also why Living Ships are not available in my download options, because they are not flown by NPC's for you to buy.

Attempting to use any version of this mod, outside of simply making a custom version that filters nothing and still forces S-class, will cause numerous crash sites to appear empty, because the mod has filtered out whatever ship type is supposed to appear at that location, and the game will not attempt to spawn something else in case of failure, which it [i]does[/i] do for NPC ships flying around. Be aware that this mod [i]does not[/i] actually make those sites unusable; removing the mod will restore whatever ship was supposed to be there.

That said, this mod [i]does not filter out Interceptors[/i], meaning it does not realistically impact hunting for them: [color=#9fc5e8]If a site is empty with this mod, it was not an Interceptor to begin with.[/color]

Good luck with your hunts, everyone!

[color=#e69138][size=6][u][font=Verdana]What This Is[/font][/u][/size][/color]

This is a mod for [i]No Man's Sky[/i], written in Lua for use with the NMS [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] mod builder, with inspiration and help from Lenni, Apex Fatality, Gumsk, Babscoole, and others from the [i]"No Man's Sky Modding"[/i] discord community. [color=#00ffff]AMUMSS is [u]required[/u] to generate this mod.[/color]

It is a [color=#6fa8dc]customizable and simple-but-powerful Ship Hunting Assistant[/color] to help people find ships they are searching for quickly, but don't want to go the route of using coordinates from other people/sources. In essence, people who enjoy finding ships themselves, and don't want to subject themselves to the punishment and pain of reloading for 3 hours at every system to find what model of Exotic lies there. In addition, [color=#6fa8dc]this mod also speeds up NPC spawning/arrival and turnover at Trading Posts and Space Stations[/color] to allow you to rapidly find the model you want. This part of the mod remains in effect no matter what ship types are selected.

The biggest advantage to this mod is that it [color=#93c47d][u]does not alter[/u] default RNG seeds[/color] used by the vanilla game to determine what models exist in each system. What this means is that [color=#93c47d]any ship you find[/color] using this mod [i]([color=#ea9999]assuming no other mods which alter seeds themselves are installed[/color])[/i] [color=#93c47d]will still exist[/color] in the system after you remove this mod. This makes it possible to rapidly find a particular ship model, and then [color=#93c47d]share those coordinates with players who do not run any mods[/color], and they will still find it in your system eventually.

Updated and working by Babscoole, with permission, credit for FLASH goes to DarkScythe though.  :)  Original FLASH page is hidden, with a link provided to this page.

[font=Verdana][size=6][color=#e69138][u]What's Customizable[/u][/color][/size][/font]

By default this mod runs in the [color=#f1c232]Exotics-only[/color] operating mode.

This means that only Exotics are capable of spawning, Freighters and other special ships aside. It also doesn't prevent your [i]own[/i] ships from spawning, nor does it lock any choices out from the Pirates or Space Sentinels. Only NPC/trader ships are filtered, since these are the ones you can actually buy ships from.

[color=#ffd966]However, this is not the only mode the mod is capable of handling.[/color]
This mod provides the option for you to [color=#93c47d]independently select any combination[/color] of the 6 base ship types in the game to allow spawning.
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/2363/2363-1657573280-1642358567.png[/img]
As you can see, toggling the ship types is as simple as changing these 6 options to [color=#93c47d]true/false[/color] and recompiling. [i]That's it![/i]
You can enable one at a time, enable specific ones, or enable all of them at once - the choice is up to you!

[color=#6fa8dc]In addition, this mod provides two other optional settings that are [color=#e06666]disabled by default[/color][color=#ffffff].[/color][/color]
The first [color=#93c47d]optional setting[/color] is to [color=#ffd966]force S-class[/color].
Looking for a specific Fighter, and don't want to spend a long time hoping for it to arrive as an S-Class? Enable Fighters, and toggle Force S-Class mode: Done!

This is [color=#e06666]disabled by default[/color] because it does have the [color=#e06666]side effect of [i]also[/i] forcing everything else[/color] to S-class, such as Freighters and Multitool cabinets. Forcing MT cabinets to S-class can be helpful for you, but will make sharing coordinates unreliable because those cabinets may not [u]normally[/u] be S class. However, it [i]can[/i] be helpful for those reloading desperately for an S-class freighter unsuccessfully. There's a secondary side effect that [color=#e06666]enabling this will force the mod to alter an additional game file, which may cause conflicts with other mods[/color] that also rely on the game file needed to force S-class spawns.

The second [color=#93c47d]optional setting[/color] is to [color=#ffd966]change spawn frequency[/color] in space.
Space has naturally lower spawns compared to planets and this setting can try and help increase those a tad.
However, I found the effects to be [color=#e06666]fairly minimal[/color] in my tests, so they also are [color=#e06666]disabled by default[/color].
You can enable it and override the frequency multipliers if you wish, but like with the above option, this will cause this mod to [color=#e06666]alter yet another game file, which may cause conflicts with other mods[/color] attempting to use the same file, for fairly little gain.

[color=#6d9eeb]Altogether, between the 6 ship types and two optional toggles, there are a whopping [color=#b6d7a8]252 possible combinations[/color] of settings for this mod.[/color]
That is a bit too many versions to maintain, that each have to be updated whenever the game updates. Therefore, I have also made this mod as easy to DIY as possible. See the section on [color=#f6b26b][u]How To Tweak/Recompile[/u][/color] further down this page.

[color=#93c47d]I am happy to provide specific versions on request[/color] for those who are uncomfortable with the process of editing and recompiling the files. Simply drop me a message on this mod page and I will see what I can do. If I find certain combinations to be very popular, I can try to maintain a limited list of a half dozen or so.

[font=Verdana][color=#e69138][u][size=6]How To Use[/size][/u][/color][/font]

[list]
[*][color=#00ff00]Creation[/color] of this mod is very simple:
[/list][list=1]
[*]Download the mod package [color=#a4c2f4]*.zip[/color] file.
[*]Process the provided Lua script through AMUMSS, to generate the mod files for the game.
[/list]
[list]
[*][color=#ff0000]Uninstalling[/color] this mod is also very simple:
[/list][list=1]
[*]Navigate into your [color=#a4c2f4]\MODS\[/color] folder.
[*]Delete or move this mods folder.
[/list][color=#00ff00] ﻿Done![/color] You can launch the game now.

Because this mod does not alter any default seeds, [color=#00ff00]ships you find and acquire using this mod will remain[/color] after this mod is removed, so there is [color=#00ff00]no worry about losing ships.[/color]

[font=Verdana][color=#f6b26b][size=5][u][color=#e69138][size=6]Usage Tips[/size][/color]
[/u][/size][/color][/font]
Be aware that this mod makes several changes to speed up the rate at which NPC traders spawn, arrive, and leave in order to facilitate more rapid cycling of ships. As a result, [color=#ffd966]NPC ships will only wait around for 15-30 seconds[/color] instead of the usual 20-60 seconds, so be mindful of that while ship hunting or they may fly away earlier than you expect them to.

At the same time, NPC's will now attempt to [color=#ffd966]fill up all landing spots[/color] on Trading Posts and Space Stations. While this is not much an issue at planetary trading posts since you can just land anywhere around it, [color=#e06666]be aware that Space Stations can fill up, and will not allow you inside[/color] - If you're not careful, you could end up crashing into the Space Station.

FInally, despite my efforts at adding more spawns, [color=#e06666]Space spawns remain much less numerous than planetary spawns[/color], so finding any trading post (trivial with an economy scanner) is recommended for ship hunting. If trying to hunt on a Space Station, and the waves seem to stop spawning, [color=#ffd966]simply fly straight out and ahead until you reach the nearest asteroid spawns[/color], then turn around and land again. This will usually cause another wave to spawn and land immediately.

[font=Verdana][size=6][color=#e69138][u]How To Tweak/Recompile[/u][/color][/size][/font]

This mod has been intentionally written in a way that should make it very easy to tweak and recompile into a new/custom version, or to update for future versions of the game if I am no longer able to maintain this mod for any reason.

[color=#ffff00]The primary requirement is to have AMUMSS working.[/color]
This may be the most difficult step of this process. Please visit [url=https://github.com/HolterPhylo/AMUMSS/releases]the github release page for AMUMSS[/url] and download a copy of the latest release in the form of a [color=#a4c2f4]*.7z[/color] file, which can be opened/extracted with [url=https://www.7-zip.org/]7-zip[/url] or similar﻿﻿ software. Be aware that AMUMSS requires specifically [color=#a4c2f4].NET8[/color] to work, at least as of this time. Links to AMUMSS' prerequisites are in their documentation; [color=#ffd966]Please follow its instructions to get it installed, updated, and running properly.[/color]

[color=#00ff00]Once AMUMSS is ready to go, the remaining steps are quite simple.[/color]
[list=1]
[*]Grab a copy of this mod's [color=#a4c2f4]Lua[/color], which I've provided here.
[*]Once you have the Lua file, place it in the [color=#a4c2f4]\AMUMSS\ModScript\[/color] folder.
[*]Run [color=#a4c2f4]BUILDMOD.BAT[/color] and follow the prompts.
[*]If you selected (Y)es to have it auto-move the compiled mod for you, then you are done. If not, copy the new mod folder from the [color=#a4c2f4]\CreatedMODS\ [/color]folder into your [i]No Man's Sky[/i] [color=#a4c2f4]\MODS\[/color] folder following the procedure from the previous How-To section.
[*]Select (Y) to [color=#a4c2f4]globally allow user input requests[/color] to change script settings during compile without needing to edit the script itself.
[/list][color=#00ff00] ﻿Done![/color] You can launch the game now.

[color=#00ffff]If you have managed to do all this, then any time you want to switch the operating mode of this mod, simply edit the first 8 toggles in the Lua again, and/or run BUILDMOD.BATand allow user input requests, then follow the prompts, and you're good to go.[/color]

[color=#e06666]If this mod becomes outdated with me unable to maintain it[/color], simply running [color=#a4c2f4]BUILDMOD.BAT[/color] on the Lua with no other changes should update the mod to work again with the latest version of the game. [color=#e06666]Only if significant changes have rendered the script full of errors should you try and read through the documentation I've left in the script itself past the first 8 toggles to try and repair it.[/color]

[font=Verdana][size=6][color=#e69138][u]Files Changed[/u][/color][/size][/font]

T[color=#a4c2f4]his mod alters the following files:[/color]
[list]
[*]METADATA\SIMULATION\SCENE\[color=#00ffff]EXPERIENCESPAWNTABLE[/color].MBIN
[*][color=#00ffff]GCAISPACESHIPGLOBALS[/color].GLOBAL.MBIN
[/list]
[color=#a4c2f4]This mod will [color=#e06666]also require[/color] the following file [color=#ffd966][i]except[/i][/color] when all ship types are enabled simultaneously, in which case this file is skipped:[/color]
[list]
[*]METADATA\SIMULATION\SPACE\[color=#00ffff]AISPACESHIPMANAGER[/color].MBIN
[/list]
[color=#a4c2f4]Finally, the two optional settings, [color=#e06666]if enabled[/color], will cause extra changes to and conflicts with other mods that use these files:[/color]
[list]
[*]METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\[color=#00ffff]INVENTORYTABLE[/color].MBIN ﻿(If [color=#ffd966]force S-class[/color] setting is enabled.)
[*][color=#00ffff]GCSOLARGENERATIONGLOBALS[/color].GLOBAL.MBIN ﻿     (If [color=#ffd966]spawn frequency multipliers[/color] are enabled.)
[/list][color=#a4c2f4]Neither of the two optional files are loaded at all if their toggles are disabled.[/color]

name: Rapid Dialogs
summary: Stop waiting for text to appear. This mod makes NPC dialogs and narrative text render near-instantly, replacing the per-language letter-by-letter delay with a minimal uniform timing. Updated for Xeno-Arena 6.3x.
author: NilOutput
description:
[b][size=6]Rapid Dialogs[/size][/b]
NMS dialog boxes type themselves out one character at a time. It's atmospheric the first time. By the hundredth NPC trade or mission briefing, you're hammering the skip button before the first sentence draws. This mod replaces the per-language punctuation delays with a single minimal delay, so text appears roughly as fast as you can read it. Tested with English.

[b][size=5]Technical Details[/size]
[/b]
Compatible with No Man's Sky version 6.33 and later. Rewrites the punctuation delay table in [font=Courier New]SPECIALTEXTPUNCTUATIONDELAYDATA.MBIN[/font] with a 0.002s delay for every alphanumeric character and common punctuation mark. No save data touched. Safe to install or remove at any time.

[b][size=5]Installation[/size]
[/b]
Install in the No Man's Sky MODS directory or via Vortex. Lua script included, so you have complete control!

[b][size=5]Acknowledgements[/size]
[/b]
Thanks to the NMS modding community — tools like AMUMSS and MBINCompiler make mods like this possible. This one's a Lua script I've been running personally for a while, now published as part of a Nexus collection. If it exactly duplicates someone else's work, that's unintentional — ping me and I'll credit or pull it.
